description: Mutated-input attack against an externally-launched HTTP/1.1 target. A seed request (GET /plaintext) is mutated by radamsa (https://gitlab.com/akihe/radamsa) into a stream of malformed HTTP/1.1 requests, each fired over a fresh TCP connection. Whatever the mutated bytes are, the target MUST NOT crash, OOM, or hang. PRIMARY CHECK: after attack window + cooldown, target serves clean GET /health with 200 OK. SECONDARY CHECK: process RSS delta within tolerance (no leaked Arenas).

attack_profile.radamsa_seed: REQUIRED — set via --radamsa-seed; without this the campaign is not reproducible
attack_profile.rate_note: requests_per_second is a REQUESTED rate. Until 2026-08-26 the driver was single-threaded and every read timeout blocked it for the full socket deadline, so the first campaign requested 500 and achieved 3.4 (60 timeouts x 2.0 s consumed the whole 120 s window; radamsa generation was 1.1 % of it). The driver now fires from a worker pool and reports achieved_rps and backlog_skips -- a run that cannot reach this rate says so instead of letting this number stand in for what happened.
attack_profile.concurrency_note: Concurrency is part of the stimulus, not a harness detail: N connections at once is a different attack from N in sequence. It travels with the result and belongs in any comparison. Sizing: rps x incomplete-mutant fraction x socket timeout gives the worker-seconds per wall second the timeouts alone consume.

tolerance.rss_note: rss_growth_pct_max is measured against a baseline taken AFTER a warm-up (baseline_warmup_seconds in the artifact). Before 2026-08-26 the baseline was cold, so first-load JIT, metaspace fill and heap commit were charged to the attack: the first slowloris run read +34.9 % against this 5 % bound while its JFR put live heap after the forced GC at 9.5 MB. RSS remains a weak leak signal here -- see comparison_axis_note -- and a run without NMT leaves the non-heap remainder unattributed. Do not compare rss_bytes_delta across runs with different baseline_warmup_seconds. Both samples are additionally preceded by a forced GC (since 2026-08-27), so the delta compares two post-collection states -- retained memory. Before that date only the FINAL sample was, which compared a collected heap against an uncollected one and biased the delta toward understating growth; on destructive-radamsa-h2 it read -588 517 376 bytes. Artifacts from before that change are not comparable with later ones.
tolerance.hang_note: hang_count counts read timeouts on mutants the target was OBLIGED to answer. Header-block termination alone is not that test: radamsa readily grows a Content-Length or a chunked Transfer-Encoding out of the header bytes, and a request announcing a body it never sends leaves the target correctly waiting -- incomplete-wait, not a hang. Counting it as complete would fail this max_hang_count: 0 against a correctly-behaved server. Since 2026-08-27 the predicate requires the announced body to be present, or the chunked stream terminated. Framing the target must REJECT rather than wait on -- a malformed or contradictory Content-Length -- still counts as owed, because a 400 is due and silence there is a finding. The H2 driver carried the same defect in frame-shaped clothing and it fired once in 400 validation iterations.

comparison_axis_note: Cross-stack radamsa results require IDENTICAL --radamsa-seed for fair comparison. Different seeds produce different inputs; comparing different seeds is meaningless. Label the seed in any cross-stack report row.
publication_mode_reason: Radamsa-mutated payloads written to disk on crash (crash-*.radamsa) contain attacker-supplied bytes; basename blocklist in publish-report.sh blocks them outside internal-only mode.
